pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (Anti-NMDA) Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The triad of rapid-onset psychiatric symptoms progressing to orofacial dyskinesias/autonomic instability, the "extreme delta brush" pattern on EEG, and an incidental mature cystic ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue expressed within the ovarian teratoma triggers the generation of autoantibodies targeting the GluN1 subunit of neuronal NMDA receptors. These IgG antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and cause cross-linking and selective internalization of cell-surface NMDA receptors in the hippocampus, forebrain, and limbic circuits. The resulting profound loss of NMDA receptor-mediated glutamatergic signaling and downstream dopaminergic disinhibition culminates in neuropsychiatric symptoms, choreiform movements, autonomic failure, central hypoventilation, and drug-resistant seizures.
